concepts_learned.title: ADLS Gen2 Hierarchical Namespace (HNS) vs Flat Blob Storage
concepts_learned.summary: HNS organizes objects into a true file system hierarchy with atomic directory operations and POSIX-compliant ACLs, replacing flat blob prefix simulation for lakehouse workloads.

concepts_learned.title: Zero-Secret Architecture via Azure System-Assigned Managed Identity
concepts_learned.summary: Eliminates credentials in code by tying identity directly to Azure Entra ID lifecycle. ADF authenticates to ADLS Gen2 and Key Vault with auto-rotated enterprise tokens.

concepts_learned.title: Azure RBAC Data Plane vs Management Plane & Least Privilege
concepts_learned.summary: Storage Blob Data Contributor and Key Vault Secrets User grant granular data-plane access without exposing administrative control or secret deletion privileges.

concepts_learned.title: ADF Git Integration & Enterprise Branching Strategy
concepts_learned.summary: Links ADF Studio to GitHub repo with collaboration branch (main), root directory (/adf), and automated ARM template publishing branch (adf_publish) for CI/CD.

concepts_learned.title: High-Watermark Metadata Pattern & State Management
concepts_learned.summary: Dedicated control table etl_watermark_control tracks high-watermark timestamp per entity. Updates occur strictly upon Copy success, preventing silent data loss.

concepts_learned.title: Hybrid Cloud Connectivity via Self-Hosted Integration Runtime (SHIR)
concepts_learned.summary: Outbound-only polling model on port 443 over TLS 1.3 extracts data securely from internal relational databases without public IPs or inbound firewall rules.

technical_questions.question: Why use System-Assigned Managed Identity over Storage Account Access Keys or SAS tokens in enterprise healthcare migrations?
technical_questions.core_rationale: Storage keys provide root-level administrative access to all data with no expiration or identity audit trail, violating HIPAA security guidelines. Managed Identity provides token-based, auditable, zero-secret access governed strictly by Entra ID RBAC.

technical_questions.question: Why is Hierarchical Namespace (HNS) mandatory for ADLS Gen2 in Medallion Lakehouse architectures instead of standard Blob Storage?
technical_questions.core_rationale: Without HNS, renaming or moving a directory requires copying every single blob individually (O(N) operations), which destroys pipeline performance at scale. HNS enables atomic metadata renames (O(1)) and granular POSIX directory ACLs.

technical_questions.question: How does a Self-Hosted Integration Runtime (SHIR) securely bridge on-premise databases without opening inbound firewall ports?
technical_questions.core_rationale: SHIR uses an outbound-only polling architecture over HTTPS port 443 with TLS 1.3. It never listens for inbound internet traffic, keeping the internal healthcare network completely secluded from external attacks.

technical_questions.question: How do you prevent data loss or duplicate ingestion if an incremental pipeline fails halfway through a run?
technical_questions.core_rationale: Through a two-phase watermark architecture where the watermark control table is only updated upon successful execution of the Copy Activity. If a failure occurs mid-batch, the old watermark remains, ensuring no records are skipped.
